title: Anthropic breaks below $83 IPO price
author: Betelbuddy
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。

comments.author: futureshock
comments.textRawHtml:
It’s possible for AI to be a transformative technology, for there to be trillions of profit to be had, for Anthropic to be the leading frontier research lab and for their stock to be a terrible investment.

We are entering uncharted waters in so many ways. You’d be a fool to put an amount of money into Anthropic that could hurt to lose.

children.author: brookst
children.textRawHtml: It’s a weird industry. It’s in high demand, but consumers are satisficed as long as they are physically transported, so there’s almost no room for differentiation, so profits are near zero. And costs are volatile with weather and fuel prices, but there’s always going to be another airline willing to roll the dice on costs not increasing, so if you charge a little more to hedge risk, you sell no tickets, and your fixed costs don’t change.

children.author: ksec
children.textRawHtml:
>It’s a weird industry.

It isn't really. Most consumer market have these problems. They are all so competitive they hardly make any money. Makes it worst when you have some form of subsidising in certain part of the supply chain.

Perhaps it is only Technology sector you get concentrated value and margin. I dont see any other sector having same problems other than luxury, but luxury is a trend not a moat. And LVMH has clearly shown that.

children.author: WheelsAtLarge
children.textRawHtml: Zero margins are what bring about innovation. Someone decides they have a new way of doing things that can be cheaper than what others have done. Airlines have shown this over and over again. My take is that this is the reason why flying is so affordable. It's affordable enough that most adults in the US can fly to the places they want to visit. It's not perfect, but over time, it seems to work.

children.author: WheelsAtLarge
children.textRawHtml: Competition from new players is what usually changes things. These days startups are what R&D used to be. A new, innovative startup comes along and changes everything. Many companies, even very profitable ones, consider R&D a drain on profits, so they cut it altogether or reduce it to a minimum.

children.author: phil21
children.textRawHtml:
Regulation is the only reason airlines are so competitive. Regulation is so effective in this area of industry that safety is very close to as optimal as current human society can provide.

After safety is taken into account, consumers pretty much only care about price. But if safety was a factor I think we would see a wildly different market.

It’s interesting to me that regulation has been so effective in this particular industry, where in most other places (healthcare as an example) you see almost the opposite outcome.

children.textRawHtml:
Indeed. And it is the reason we only have three major carriers in the US, plus some regional carriers and low-cost carriers.

Eventually the market reaches an equilibrium where the remaining carriers have enough margin to survive (and everyone starts unironically complaining about the lack of competition).
